taxYearRuns: 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2026 (calendar-year taxpayers; returns filed in 2027)
jurisdiction: United States — federal only. State income tax, state unemployment insurance and local taxes are out of scope.
refreshRule: Re-verify when the IRS publishes the tax-year-2027 inflation adjustments (normally mid/late October), the 2027 retirement-plan limits (normally early/mid November) and when SSA publishes the 2027 COLA/wage base (normally mid-October; Federal Register notice follows in late October/early November). Until then these 2026 figures are final.
verificationMethod: Every figure was read on verifiedDate from the primary document named in its `source` (IRS Revenue Procedure / Notice PDFs and irs.gov pages fetched with curl, User-Agent databutler-curation/1.0; all returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-03). The `quote` field reproduces the sentence or table row the value was taken from. `previous` values come from the 2025 counterpart document named in `previousSource` or from the same page where it states the prior-year figure. Figures were never written from memory and were not copied from any third-party calculator or from the LifeByNumbers app.py — disagreements with app.py are listed in NOTES.md. Figures added on 2026-10-31 carry that verifiedDate and were read that day: ssa.gov, cms.gov, medicare.gov, ecfr.gov and federalregister.gov in a browser, irs.gov with curl. The file-level verifiedDate stays the oldest figure's date until every figure has been re-read; each figure's own verifiedDate is authoritative. Rule pages that state no start date use the first day of the period served, or of the publication edition read.
licence: Works of the United States federal government (IRS, SSA, CMS, Medicare.gov, eCFR, Federal Register) are in the public domain under 17 U.S.C. § 105. Figures are reproduced with their source URL; no third-party content is included.

medicare.scope: No wage base limit. Additional Medicare Tax thresholds are statutory (not indexed) and apply to the sum of wages, RRTA compensation and self-employment income.

figures.quote: The Medicare tax rate is 1.45% each for the employee and employer, unchanged from 2025. There is no wage base limit for Medicare tax.

figures.label: Net Investment Income Tax rate
figures.quote: Effective Jan. 1, 2013, individual taxpayers are liable for a 3.8 percent Net Investment Income Tax on the lesser of their net investment income, or the amount by which their modified adjusted gross income exceeds the statutory threshold amount based on their filing status.

figures.label: Net Investment Income Tax MAGI threshold: married filing jointly
figures.quote: The statutory threshold amounts are: Married filing jointly — $250,000

figures.label: Net Investment Income Tax MAGI threshold: married filing separately
figures.quote: The statutory threshold amounts are: Married filing separately — $125,000

figures.label: Net Investment Income Tax MAGI threshold: single or head of household
figures.quote: The statutory threshold amounts are: Single or head of household — $200,000

figures.label: Net Investment Income Tax MAGI threshold: qualifying widow(er) with a child
figures.quote: The statutory threshold amounts are: Qualifying widow(er) with a child — $250,000
